title: Ukraine and the Council of Europe sign the agreement establishing a Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression
body:
On 25 June 2025, in Strasbourg, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Council of Europe Secretary General Alain Berset signed the agreement establishing the Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine. The agreement includes the tribunal's statute. The European External Action Service published its account of the signing on 1 July 2025.

The tribunal is to be set up within the Council of Europe framework to investigate, prosecute and try Russian political and military leaders who bear the greatest responsibility for the crime of aggression against Ukraine. It is meant to address a jurisdictional gap, since the International Criminal Court does not currently have jurisdiction over the crime of aggression.

Zelenskyy stressed at the signing that every Russian war criminal faces justice, including Putin. The tribunal is separate from the ICC, which continues to pursue war crimes and crimes against humanity, including the warrants issued in 2023 and 2024. The Council of Europe also hosts the Register of Damage for Ukraine, which records claims for compensation, so that the three mechanisms address, respectively, the leadership crime of aggression, individual war crimes and civil compensation.
